items.exemplar:
A. The map shows Columbus sailing steadily farther south and west with each voyage: the first lands in the Bahamas, while the third and fourth reach the South American mainland and Central America. The pattern reveals a deliberate, crown-sponsored program of exploration pushing deeper into unknown territory rather than a single accidental landfall.

B. For Native Americans the voyages were catastrophic. European diseases such as smallpox, to which Native peoples had no immunity, ravaged populations across the Caribbean and the mainland. The Spanish also imposed the encomienda system, forcing Native peoples into plantation labor and wiping out communities that resisted.

C. For Europeans the voyages opened access to the wealth of a new hemisphere. Silver and gold from Central and South America flowed to Spain, and new crops — potatoes, maize, tobacco — entered European diets and agriculture. The voyages also launched the Columbian Exchange of plants, animals, diseases, and ideas that permanently altered both continents.
parts: A. Identify and briefly explain ONE pattern in European exploration shown by the routes on the map.
B. Briefly explain ONE way Columbus's voyages transformed life for Native Americans.
C. Briefly explain ONE way Columbus's voyages transformed life for Europeans.
items.stimulus: The following map shows the routes of Christopher Columbus's four voyages to the Americas, 1492–1504. The first voyage (1492–1493) sails from Spain to the Bahamas and the northern coast of Hispaniola. The second (1493–1496) reaches Dominica and explores the Caribbean islands. The third (1498–1500) sails farther south, touching the coast of present-day Venezuela in South America. The fourth (1502–1504) follows the coast of Central America from Honduras to Panama.
